title: Bonita Yacht
description:
Bonita Yacht is a strong value oriented Galapagos cruise option for travelers who want a comfortable small yacht without luxury pricing. It works well for couples, families, solo travelers, and small groups that prioritize itinerary, wildlife access, and friendly onboard service.

The yacht offers classic social areas, including a dining room, lounge, bar, hot drinks and purified water station, and a sun deck with ocean views. Cabins are practical and comfortable, generally equipped with private bathrooms, air conditioning, and flexible bedding.

Bonita operates three main itineraries, including a longer western route and shorter southern and northern routes. Published routes include Santa Cruz, Santiago, Isabela, Fernandina, Floreana, Española, San Cristóbal, Genovesa or replacement sites, North Seymour, South Plaza, and Black Turtle Cove.

title: Galaxy Sirius
description:
The Galaxy Sirius is a luxury expedition catamaran recognized for its sleek black hulls and an elegant, refined travel experience designed for small groups. It accommodates up to 16 guests across 9 cabins, supported by a crew of 9 and 2 bilingual naturalist guides, with Wi-Fi available onboard.

The onboard experience blends premium comfort with nature exploration: panoramic views from cabins and balconies, a sundeck, jacuzzi, lounges, a bar, a boutique and reading corners. Throughout the voyage, guests enjoy local gastronomy while taking part in activities such as snorkeling, kayaking, panga rides, paddle boarding and guided hikes.

Galaxy Sirius offers three itinerary options: the Southern Route (5 days/4 nights), the Western Route (6 days/5 nights) and the Northern Route (6 days/5 nights). The Southern Route, featured here, focuses on San Cristobal, Espanola, Floreana, Santa Fe, South Plaza and Santa Cruz, combining beaches, cliffs, snorkeling sites, seabird colonies, sea lion encounters and a visit to the Charles Darwin Research Station. Highlight species along this route include frigatebirds, penguins, land iguanas, sharks, sea lions, giant tortoises and rays.

title: Galaxy Diver II
description:
Galaxy Diver II is built for travelers whose main goal is scuba diving in the Galapagos Marine Reserve. Unlike naturalist only cruises, this vessel focuses on liveaboard diving access to remote and high impact underwater sites, especially Wolf and Darwin Islands.

The onboard layout supports dive operations with dedicated equipment areas, a dive platform, modern cabins, and social areas for meals and rest between dives. It is best suited to certified divers who want repeated immersion opportunities in one of the world’s most famous marine environments.

Routes commonly include Baltra, Punta Carrion, Wolf Island, Darwin Island, Fernandina or replacement marine sites depending on conservation rules, Isabela, Cousin Rock, and Santa Cruz Highlands. Published routes mention hammerheads, whale sharks, Galapagos sharks, rays, sea lions, turtles, penguins, and other pelagic species.
